name: INNERGY
description: Job software for architectural woodworking and high-end millwork shops. It covers the lead, the estimate, the project, the shop floor, and the install. Marc Sanderson and a partner bought a Minnesota woodworking shop in 1997, built the tool for themselves, then sold it as a product.

mentions.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, May 2026. About $25M revenue in 2025, growing more than 50% a year, and he expects to approach $40M in 2026. Sold 51% to Mainsail Partners in 2025 for more than $40M. He stayed CEO. Bootstrapped for years on the shop's profits before the growth-equity deal. Retention about 95%.
mentions.indieAngle: A craft shop that still runs the job in a spreadsheet and an old drawing program.

whyItPrints: A custom shop's estimate, the cut list, and the install date do not fit a generic system. Once they live here, switching is brutal. He says retention is about 95%, and that teaching the shops is part of why they stay.
whyThisMatters:
INNERGY is the job system for a shop that builds custom architectural woodwork. The lead, the estimate, the drawings, the shop floor, and the install are in one place. The founder bought a Minnesota shop in 1997 with a partner, built the tool for that shop, and then sold the tool.

He says 2025 was about twenty-five million, growing more than fifty percent a year, toward something closer to forty million in 2026. He sold a majority stake in 2025 for more than forty million and stayed CEO. Years of that were funded by the shop's own profits. Retention around ninety-five percent, and he treats teaching the other shops as part of the product. May 2026 interview. Self-reported.

You pay so the estimate and the cut list are the same system.
